methods: Video (928x576 px, 12.5 fps, 10.0 min; sha256 e260161876eb) of 1 mouse in a 45 x 45 cm arena was analysed with Kappa 0.1.0 (protocol sha256 28a0d7d0a713, confirmed by Yehor Ivashchenko via the kappa command line). Each mouse was segmented and tracked with sam3.1_multiplex@0567debeec80 (self-hosted, sam3@f1647e8d0c1d, kappa-sam v3) from the text prompt "mouse", and positions were converted to centimetres with a four-point homography of the arena floor. Trajectories were smoothed with a median filter (0.2 s window). Zones were defined as a centre zone covering 50% of the floor area. A subject was counted inside a zone when at least 70% of its body area was inside it. Behaviour bouts were detected frame by frame with kappa-rearing/25638bb84dc1 on sam-3.1 silhouettes, split by the body centre's distance to the nearest wall where the protocol asks for it. Definitions: Rearing: The mouse lifts both forepaws off the floor and stands up on its hind legs, free-standing or with its forepaws against the wall. Supported rearing: A rear whose body centre is within 12.5 cm of a wall at mid-bout, the convention of the original TSE set-up. Unsupported rearing: A rear whose body centre is more than 12.5 cm from every wall at mid-bout. Of 9 reported values, 9 were verified, 0 were withheld because the underlying track failed an integrity check, and 0 were refused as not measurable.

body.notes: The evaluation protocol, fixed before the test set was analysed. The centre zone is the central 50% of the floor, as in the TSE system the paper compares against. Arena corners are located on a keyframe of each video by perception grounding. Videos are analysed at 12.5 frames per second (every other frame), which keeps every rear several frames long.
body.question: How far does the mouse travel in each 5-minute bin, how long does it spend in the centre and how often does it enter it, how long is it immobile, and how often does it rear (all rears, and supported vs unsupported)?
body.title: Open field test, Sturman et al. (2020) set-up, 45 x 45 cm arena

findings.claim: The centre zone is not the conventional, TSE-comparable centre it is claimed to be.
findings.suggestion: State the comparator's centre dimensions in centimetres, redefine the zone to match them exactly, clarify whether '50%' is linear or areal, and recompute both centre metrics.
findings.why: The result parameters define the centre by zone_area_fraction=0.5. In the 45 x 45 cm arena that is a 31.8 x 31.8 cm square, leaving only about 6.6 cm between the centre boundary and each wall, roughly one mouse body length. An animal close to the wall can therefore be scored as in the centre. This inflates the reported 162.64 s and 61 entries relative to a centre defined as 50% of the linear dimensions (22.5 x 22.5 cm, 25% of the area), and the record does not establish that the areal definition matches the TSE convention invoked in the protocol notes.

findings.claim: Centre occupancy and entries use a nonstandard 70%-of-body rule with no minimum dwell.
findings.suggestion: Use the paradigm's tracked-point entry rule, or provide a justification and sensitivity analysis comparing body-fraction and point-based scoring; add a non-zero minimum dwell or hysteresis for entries.
findings.why: The protocol and result parameters require at least 70% of the segmented body area to be inside the zone (entry_body_fraction=0.7) and set min_dwell_s=0.0. Occupancy therefore depends on posture, orientation and mask quality, and entries will be delayed or suppressed relative to centre-point scoring. Conversely, with no dwell requirement, one qualifying 0.08 s frame can register an entry. The reported 162.64 s and 61 entries are consequently not interpretable as conventional centre-point measures without validation.

findings.claim: 'Supported' rearing is inferred from an overly broad wall-proximity proxy that cannot establish forepaw support.
findings.suggestion: Score forepaw-wall contact from a view capable of observing it, or rename the measures as near-wall and away-from-wall rears; in either case re-derive the split using a physically reach-plausible criterion.
findings.why: A rear is classified as supported when the body centre is within 12.5 cm of a wall at mid-bout. In a 45 cm arena, only the central 20 x 20 cm, 19.8% of the floor, is more than 12.5 cm from every wall, so 80.2% of positions are eligible to be called supported. A body centre 12.5 cm from a wall is beyond plausible forepaw reach from the centre of the body, so proximity does not establish the wall contact implied by 'supported'. The resulting 85 supported versus 2 unsupported rears out of 87 is therefore largely determined by the threshold geometry. The top-down silhouette detector also cannot directly observe forepaws leaving the floor or contacting a wall.

findings.claim: The rearing counts include low-confidence, very brief bouts and do not document the adjudication required by the protocol.
findings.suggestion: State a behaviour-confidence threshold and minimum bout duration, provide the per-bout adjudication record, and report a sensitivity analysis excluding low-confidence and sub-0.5 s bouts.
findings.why: All three rearing behaviours are marked adjudicate=true, but every listed bout has an empty rationale and is attributed only to the automated detector; no per-bout adjudication outcome is documented. No behaviour-specific confidence threshold is defined, yet numerous counted bouts have confidences below 0.5, including 0.361, 0.389, 0.393, 0.405 and 0.411. Several bouts span only about three frames at 12.5 fps, approximately 0.24 s, including frames 2224-2227, 2651-2654, 3094-3097 and 3910-3913. One of only two unsupported rears is the three-frame bout at frames 2224-2227, making unsupported_rears=2 especially sensitive to these inclusion rules. Nevertheless all three counts are marked verified.

findings.claim: The methods paragraph lacks the animal, session, calibration and detector-validation information needed to interpret the results.
findings.suggestion: Add complete animal and testing details, arena and camera calibration errors, and validation of the rearing detector against blinded human scoring in this arena and camera view.
findings.why: The record identifies the subject only as one 'mouse': no strain, sex, age, weight, housing, habituation, testing time, illumination, arena wall properties or cleaning procedure is reported. It also gives no camera height or viewing geometry and no homography or corner-localisation error for the single-keyframe arena calibration. For the novel kappa-rearing detector applied to top-down silhouettes, no sensitivity, specificity, accuracy or comparison with human scoring is supplied. Without these details, the credibility and reproducibility of 87 rears in 600 s, 69.92 s immobility and the centre measures cannot be assessed.

withheld: Locked and refused results carry no value, evidence or uncertainty here, and behaviour bouts are listed only for a subject whose every result for that behaviour is verified: a locked number is not defensible until its integrity events are settled, and a locked count is just its bouts counted. The full manifest kept for audit is the file at `path`, sha256 `manifest_sha256`.
